lead: Being a responsible tourist in Valencia takes no effort: it is small everyday decisions that add up. Here are the commitments you can adopt during your stay to leave a positive footprint.

If you get around sustainably, consume consciously and practise responsible tourism, you are already actively contributing to the conservation of Valencia for the generations to come. These nine commitments will cost you no effort, but they will have a real impact on the city, its nature and its residents.
Each commitment explained with concrete actions you can take during your stay.

items.title: Use water and energy responsibly
items.body: In your accommodation, do not change the towels every day if it is not necessary. Avoid long baths. Turn off the air conditioning when you leave the room. In Valencia, tap water is completely drinkable: you do not need to buy bottled water. The PUSDAR fountains spread across the city offer filtered, chilled water free of charge.
bullets: Reuse towels for several days
Tap water in Valencia is drinkable · Use it
Refill your bottle at the 50+ free PUSDAR fountains
Turn off lights and air conditioning when you leave your accommodation

items.title: Minimise waste and eliminate plastic
items.body: Always carry a reusable bag for shopping at markets and shops. Avoid single-use plastic bottles by using the city’s filtered water fountains. In Valencia you will find clearly differentiated recycling bins in the usual colours on every street and square. Used cooking oil has specific containers spread across the city.
bullets: Cloth bag for shopping at markets and shops
Reusable bottle instead of single-use plastic
Recycle in the coloured bins on every street
Used oil has its own recycling containers

items.title: Get around without a car: on foot, by bike or on public transport
items.body: Valencia is completely flat, with more than 160 km of cycle lanes and a historic centre that is mostly pedestrian. The Valenbisi system has 276 stations with 2,750 bikes available 24 hours a day. The EMT bus network, the metro and the tram connect every point of interest. The Tourist Card includes unlimited transport from €15.30 and is the smartest option for a stay of 2–3 days.
bullets: The historic centre is pedestrian: you do not need a car
Valenbisi: 276 stations · 30 min free per journey
Tourist Card: unlimited transport from €15.30
Metro L3/L5 from the airport: 25 min and €1.50

items.title: Eat local, regional food
items.body: Valencian cuisine is built on its own huerta and the Mediterranean as a direct pantry. Eating in restaurants that work with seasonal, kilometre 0 produce is the tastiest and most sustainable way to get to know the city. The municipal markets are the best place to buy fresh food without industrial packaging. Look for DO Valencia rice, Utiel-Requena wine and horchata from Alboraya.
bullets: Menu of the day in neighbourhood restaurants: €10–15 with everything
Municipal markets: fresh produce without plastic
DO Valencia and DO Utiel-Requena wine: local quality
Valencian paella in El Palmar: the most authentic and km 0

items.title: Buy from small shops and local crafts
items.body: Every euro spent in a local shop, a municipal market or a Valencian artisan has an economic impact on the city several times greater than the same euro spent in a large franchise. Manises ceramics, handcrafted fans, Ensedarte’s hand-painted silk or produce from the huerta are authentic souvenirs with a story. El Carmen, the Central Market and the Plaza Redonda are the best places for responsible shopping.
bullets: Manises and Paterna ceramics: a tradition of 800 years
Handcrafted fans in the historic centre
Central Market: produce straight from the huerta
Avoid souvenirs made outside Spain

items.title: Enjoy natural areas with respect
items.body: The Albufera Natural Park, the beaches of El Saler and La Devesa, and the natural parks in the interior of the province are fragile ecosystems that require conscious behaviour. Not entering restricted areas, staying on marked paths, not disturbing wildlife and not leaving waste are the basic rules of responsible ecotourism. To get to these places, use the bus or a bike, not the car.
bullets: Stay on the marked paths in natural parks
Do not leave waste on natural beaches or dunes
Watch birds from the observatories without getting close
Bus 24 or 25 to the Albufera: free with the Tourist Card

items.title: Protect the Mediterranean’s marine wildlife
items.body: The Mediterranean that bathes Valencia is home to the loggerhead turtle (Caretta caretta), the bottlenose dolphin, Posidonia oceanica and other protected species. If you find a loggerhead turtle or another species on the beach or in the sea that seems to need help, the most effective thing is to call 112 to activate the Stranding Network. Do not touch or handle the animal: the experts will know how best to help it.
bullets: If you find an injured turtle on the beach: call 112
Do not anchor in Posidonia oceanica meadows
Do not feed or handle wild marine fauna
Use sunscreens free of oxybenzone and octinoxate

items.title: Respect local culture and neighbours’ rest
items.body: Valencians have their own hours, customs and spaces. Night-time rest starts early in residential neighbourhoods: avoid noise after 22:00 in areas not intended for leisure. Respect sacred spaces and festival rituals. Learn a few words in Valencian and in Spanish: attitude and effort are always welcome. Markets, parks and public transport are spaces shared with residents.
bullets: Avoid noise in residential areas after 22:00
Respect the rituals and spaces of local festivals
Markets are neighbours’ spaces, not just tourist ones
Learn: “gràcies” and “bon dia” open many doors

items.title: Go paperless and travel digital
items.body: Visit Valencia makes online and downloadable editions of all its guides, maps and tourist plans available to every traveller, with no need to print anything. Download the maps to your phone before you arrive to use them offline. Keep your tickets digital. Use the transport apps instead of physical tickets. Every small paperless decision adds up.
bullets: Downloadable guides and maps of Valencia at visitvalencia.com
Museum and attraction tickets in digital format
EMT and Valenbisi apps: no physical ticket
400+ free WiFi points to connect without using data

items: Tap water in Valencia: completely drinkable and of good quality · Free PUSDAR fountains across the city

Recycle: coloured bins on every street · Used oil has specific containers
Eat in neighbourhood restaurants: menu of the day €10–15 · Produce from the huerta and the Mediterranean
Injured wildlife on the coast: call 112 · Mediterranean Stranding Network
